content.title: About
content.content: Almond paste is a thick blend of ground almonds and sugar, sometimes enriched with oil or eggs. It has a sweet, nutty flavor and is used in confectionery as a filling for cakes, cookies, marzipan and other desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Almond paste is the base of traditional marzipan, popular across Europe and the Middle East.
Unlike almond butter, paste retains fine almond particles, giving it a denser texture.
There are two main types: sweet (high sugar) and unsweetened (for a more neutral taste).
It is often used in gluten‑free recipes as a flour substitute.
In Italy, almond paste is traditionally served with panettone during the holidays.

items.title: Rich in vitamin E
items.content: Almond paste retains much of the vitamin E found in almonds, an antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Provides healthy monounsaturated fats
items.content: Monounsaturated fats support heart health and can improve lipid profiles.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Provides protein and fiber
items.content: The paste supplies plant protein and dietary fiber, helping promote satiety.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: It contains calcium, important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Almond paste can trigger allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to nuts.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Because of its fat and sugar content, portion sizes should be moderated.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The sweet version may raise blood glucose levels, so people with diabetes should opt for unsweetened paste.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Almonds contain oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Almond paste is used as a filling for cakes, cupcakes, cookies, in marzipan, as well as in creams and glazes. It can be mixed with fruit purées, added to dough, or melted for drizzling over desserts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the paste in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 months. For longer storage, freeze it for up to 6 months. Before use, check for off‑odors or signs of spoilage.
